key_insight: The paper shows that the optimality conditions for stochastic control in Itô and rough path formalisms are linked by a conditional expectation bridge, making the two PMP adjoint systems mathematically compatible.
engineering_relevance: This unification can simplify how engineers derive and implement stochastic control algorithms, including learning-based model fine-tuning and indirect shooting for feedback control.
method: Derives a rough-path stochastic Pontryagin Maximum Principle for adapted controls without forward-backward SDEs
Uses stochastic needle variations to extend rough-control optimality theory
Connects Itô and rough adjoints via Itô–Stratonovich conversion and forward/backward duality identities
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two concrete applications—adjoint matching for generative model fine-tuning and an indirect shooting method for feedback problems—as validation of the theory.
watch_item: The bridge relies on conditional expectations and framework-specific regularity assumptions, so practical use may be sensitive to filtration, adaptiveness, and numerical approximation details.
paper_title: Unified Optimality Conditions for Stochastic Optimal Control in the Rough Path and Itô Frameworks
